results.question: What does Volkswagen disclose about employee health and safety in 2024?
results.ground_truth: Chapter 1.7 of our Social Charter states in case of Occupational Safety and Health Protection: Volkswagen meets at least the respective national standards for a safe and hygienic working environment and in this context will undertake appropriate measures to assure health and safety in the workplace so that healthy employment conditions are assured.
results.answer:
Block 1 (key takeaway): Volkswagen discloses that occupational health and safety is a key sustainability topic addressed through Group policies, ISO 45001 certification requirements, and systematic risk analysis. The company reports on training hours per employee and conducts regular audits to monitor compliance and effectiveness.

Block 2 (detailed answer): According to Volkswagen's 2024 Sustainability Report, the company addresses occupational health and safety in accordance with ESRS 1 standards [Volkswagen's 2024 Sustainability Report, p. 156]. The Group has established a policy ensuring senior managers allocate adequate resources for occupational health and safety initiatives, including financial, human, and material support [Volkswagen's 2024 Sustainability Report, p. 156]. Volkswagen AG's Group Occupational Health and Safety organizational unit handles standard-setting, information provision, communication, and monitoring [Volkswagen's 2024 Sustainability Report, p. 156]. The company requires ISO 45001 management system certification for all production sites with more than 1,000 employees, with completion targeted by 2026 [Volkswagen's 2024 Sustainability Report, p. 156]. In 2024, four Group audits were conducted based on ISO 45001 requirements and Group policies [Volkswagen's 2024 Sustainability Report, p. 156]. Additionally, the company conducted a systematic health & safety risk analysis using self-assessment questionnaires across Group companies [Volkswagen's 2024 Sustainability Report, p. 156]. Regarding training, the average number of training hours per employee according to ESRS requirements was 18.9 hours [Volkswagen's 2024 Sustainability Report, p. 156].

Block 3 (Evidence excerpts):
"Actions related to occupational health and safety A Group policy ensures that the senior managers of each company make adequate financial, human and material resources available to fulfill the tasks in the focus area of occupational health and safety" [Volkswagen's 2024 Sustainability Report, p. 156]
"The Group has issued a Group-wide policy requiring the companies to introduce and obtain certification for an ISO 45001 management system at all production sites with more than 1,000 employees" [Volkswagen's 2024 Sustainability Report, p. 156]
"Four (three) Group audits were conducted in 2024" [Volkswagen's 2024 Sustainability Report, p. 156]
"As a result, it was possible to identify improvement potential and introduce measures to reduce sustainability-related risks" [Volkswagen's 2024 Sustainability Report, p. 156]
"The average number of training hours per employee in accordance with the requirements of the ESRS was 18.9 hours" [Volkswagen's 2024 Sustainability Report, p. 156]

**Limitations**
The provided context does not contain specific data on employee injury rates, workplace accident statistics, or detailed health and safety performance metrics beyond the general framework and training hours. Information on actual incident reporting, fatalities, or serious injuries is absent. The disclosure focuses primarily on policy frameworks and procedural compliance rather than outcome-based health and safety performance indicators. While ISO 45001 certification is mentioned, there are no details on certification status or audit outcomes for individual facilities. The context lacks specific targets, baselines, or measurable outcomes for health and safety improvements.
